scope: Selected GRIN2A/GRIN2B variants for an expert-reviewable NMDAR reduced-function research cluster. This is a selected evidence set, not a complete variant catalog or clinical classification.
selection_rule: Core requires a reported Likely LoF integrated category and primary measured receptor evidence with WT comparator. Possible LoF remains provisional. Opposing and unresolved controls remain separate. Pathogenicity alone does not qualify.

sources.title: Mechanistic Insight into NMDA Receptor Dysregulation by Rare Variants in the GluN2A and GluN2B Agonist Binding Domains
sources.role: Primary functional study; Tables 2–3 and supplementary clinical/variant tables.

sources.title: Positive allosteric modulators that target NMDA receptors rectify loss-of-function GRIN variants associated with neurological and neuropsychiatric disorders

sources.title: Classification of missense variants in the N-methyl-d-aspartate receptor GRIN gene family as gain- or loss-of-function

sources.title: Functional effects of disease-associated variants reveal that the S1-M1 linker of the NMDA receptor critically controls channel opening
sources.role: Primary pre-M1 functional study; Tables 1–4 include clinical/variant information, assays and modeled charge-transfer ratios.

sources.title: De novo GRIN variants in M3 helix associated with neurological disorders control channel gating of NMDA receptor
sources.role: Primary M3 functional study; Tables 1–3 and figures. Assays use diheteromeric GluN1/GluN2 receptors.

sources.title: Opportunities for Precision Treatment of GRIN2A and GRIN2B Gain-of-Function Variants in Triheteromeric N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptors
sources.role: Primary pharmacology in engineered triheteromeric receptors; context evidence for GRIN2B-A639V. It tests antagonist response and glutamate/glycine potency, not a complete triheteromeric LoF/GoF charge-transfer classification.

functional_evidence.evidence_location: Results, 'GRIN Variants Selected for Rescue Pharmacology in Triheteromeric NMDARs'; Supplemental Table S2; Table 1.
functional_evidence.assay: Glutamate and glycine potency in diheteromeric receptors; channel-blocker response in engineered GluN1/GluN2A/GluN2B triheteromeric receptors.

functional_evidence.triheteromeric_context: Variant-containing receptors were tested for inhibitor response; this is not a full multi-assay or synaptic charge-transfer LoF/GoF classification.

integrated_function.source_classification: Gain-of-function in the tested receptor assay
integrated_function.evidence_location: Figure 5/Table 3 summary; charge-transfer ratios 7.9 and 6.2 of WT.
integrated_function.why: Both author-calculated charge-transfer ratios and several functional parameters are above WT in the tested diheteromeric assay. A separate engineered-triheteromeric study also reports enhanced agonist potency, but tests pharmacological inhibitor response rather than complete net function.

context_caveats: The reduced surface-expression ratio coexists with increased gating, potency and modeled charge transfer; do not interpret one parameter alone as net LoF.
Triheteromeric receptor results depend on engineered stoichiometry and construct context; no neuronal or clinical effect is established.
